rows.title: Policy
rows.read: Britain's hot inflation figure all but settles a Bank of England hike in November, and Australian hike bets kept rising. Canada and New Zealand are also expected to raise rates next week, while the Fed waits until December. Currencies whose central banks are about to act keep the rate edge.
rows.figure: BoE Nov 5 hike ~95–98%, Dec ~51%; BoC Oct 28 ~93%; RBNZ Oct 28 ~80%; RBA Nov 3 ~42%; Fed Oct hold ~85%, Dec hike ~90%; ECB Dec ~76%; BoJ Dec ~80%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: US housing stays weak under high mortgage rates, and UK house prices grew at their slowest pace since March. None of it moved rate bets today, because central banks are watching inflation, not growth.
rows.figure: UK house prices +0.9% y/y in Aug (1.7% fc); US pending home sales −7.3% in Sep; Japan Sep exports +16.7% y/y (~+20% fc)

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: UK inflation rose more than expected as fuel costs fed through, and German producer prices also ran hot, so the oil shock is still lifting prices. That keeps central banks leaning toward hikes. Coming up: New Zealand's inflation report at 4:45 PM CT tonight and Japan's on Thursday evening.
rows.figure: UK CPI Sep 3.5% y/y (3.4% fc); German PPI +6.7% y/y (6.2% fc); NZ Q3 CPI fc 3.8% y/y, 4:45 PM CT; Japan core CPI fc 2.1%, Thu 6:30 PM CT

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: Iran's hard line and more US warships raised tension in the Gulf, but markets stayed calm and safe-haven currencies got no extra lift. The real stress point is France, where borrowing costs hit their highest in more than 20 years.
rows.figure: France 10-year >5% (first since 2002), gap over Germany ~153bp; US 20-year auction 5.469% (record); dollar index ~101.7, flat

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: Oil rose in the morning and gave it back after Washington moved to ease supply, ending near $109. Prices that high still help exporters like Canada and cost importers like Japan, the euro area and Britain. Europe's gas bill climbed too.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, even as a Bank of Canada hike looks likely, which leaves those bets exposed if the loonie keeps rising. They also bet against the kiwi and the euro. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against EUR and NZD (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), strongly for gold (trimmed); oil bets near weakest since 2015

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: France's borrowing costs rose above 5%, a sign investors want more to hold French debt before Moody's review on Friday and a budget vote on October 27. In Britain, borrowing ran above forecast a week before the budget, leaving less room for help with energy bills.
